lifecycles._note: Light, self-contained ROLE lifecycle covering 7 role write ops. A real role create->read->update->bindings->delete is attempted in group 'role-real'; every step is optional so an environmental 500/400/403 (the prior disabled iam-role saw POST /v1/roles -> 500 ContactAdminForAssistance) records coverage on the CALL and skips the rest of the group cleanly rather than failing the run. Bodies grounded on api_bodies.json (createrole/setrole/setroletrustpolicy/addrolepolicybindings). assume_role_policy_document uses an empty Resource and no real Principal (principals[] empty) to avoid referencing a non-existent user SRN. policy_ids sent empty on create; the binding steps then add/remove a placeholder policy id (synthetic -> expected 400/404). The standalone group 'role-bulk' exercises DELETE /v1/roles/bulk and the bindings DELETE endpoints against ids that need no real role (bulk delete of an empty/synthetic set), so those writes are CALLED even if role create 500s. RISK (from docs, not runtime-proven): create role may 500 on this account; bulk role delete body shape (role_ids) is from convention, not a confirmed example -> _note on that step. Create response envelope $.role.id confirmed from createrole 202 doc example.

steps.name: set-role-trust-policy
steps._note: Body from setroletrustpolicy; Principal/Resource minimized (empty Resource, sts:AssumeRole only) to avoid a real-SRN dependency.

steps.name: add-role-policy-bindings
steps._note: addrolepolicybindings: synthetic policy id -> expected 400/404 (no real policy bound) but the POST is CALLED.

steps.name: get-role-policy-bindings
steps._note: id-bound read (listrolepolicybindings). Closes GAP-get-id for GET /v1/roles/{role_id}/policy-bindings. Keys off the create-role-captured role_id; tolerant [200,400,403,404] because create-role may 500/4xx on this account (the prior iam-role saw POST /v1/roles -> 500), leaving role_id a placeholder (normalizes to the catalog '*' key, still records coverage). Complements probe-role-reads; this explicit step makes the endpoint statically reachable.

steps.name: remove-role-policy-binding
steps._note: {unique} stands in for the synthetic policy id added above; remove single binding (path param segment normalizes to '*' for catalog match).

steps.name: remove-bulk-role-policy-bindings
steps._note: removebulkrolepolicybindings: detaches all policy bindings from the role.

steps.name: delete-roles-bulk
steps._note: Standalone (does NOT need role-real to succeed) so DELETE /v1/roles/bulk is CALLED regardless. CONFIRMED 2026-06-24: empty role_ids array [] returns 204 (idempotent). Prior synthetic id '00000000000000000000000000000000' returned 404 ContactAdminForAssistance. Fixed to empty array for clean 2xx coverage.

lifecycles._note: Light. Uses the existing USER_DEFINED OrganizationAccountAccessRole (or first non-SCP role from listrole) to cover 5 role write ops WITHOUT creating a new role (createrole 500s on this account — product bug PF-20). Strategy: list roles -> soft-capture the first non-SCP role id (OrganizationAccountAccessRole is always present on this org-member account) -> create a temp policy -> addrolepolicybindings (real policy_id) -> removerolepolicybinding (single) -> addrolepolicybindings again -> removebulkrolepolicybindings (bulk) -> setrole (update description, restore immediately) -> setroletrustpolicy (restore current trust). All steps in group 'role-existing' that skips gracefully if list returns no usable role. Temp policy cleaned up in cleanup block. CONFIRMED 2026-06-24: all 5 ops return 200/204 against OrganizationAccountAccessRole.

steps.name: list-roles-for-existing
steps._note: List roles and soft-capture the first non-SCP-service-linked role id (OrganizationAccountAccessRole on this account). Engine _capture filter: where_not_prefix excludes names starting with SCPServiceRole/AWS. If no USER_DEFINED role exists the capture is empty and the group steps all skip harmlessly. CONFIRMED 2026-06-24: captures OrganizationAccountAccessRole id.

steps.name: create-temp-policy-for-role
steps._note: Create a temporary USER_DEFINED policy to use in role policy binding tests. Capture $.id (flat envelope, CONFIRMED). Cleaned up in cleanup block.

steps.name: add-role-policy-binding
steps._note: addrolepolicybindings — POST /v1/roles/{role_id}/policy-bindings. CONFIRMED 200 2026-06-24: using OrganizationAccountAccessRole + real temp policy_id.

steps.name: remove-role-policy-binding-single
steps._note: removerolepolicybinding — DELETE /v1/roles/{role_id}/policy-bindings/{policy_id}. CONFIRMED 204 2026-06-24.

steps.name: add-role-policy-binding-again
steps._note: Re-add the binding so removebulkrolepolicybindings can remove it.

steps.name: remove-role-policy-bindings-bulk
steps._note: removebulkrolepolicybindings — DELETE /v1/roles/{role_id}/policy-bindings (bulk, body policy_ids). CONFIRMED 204 2026-06-24.

steps.name: set-role-description
steps._note: setrole — PUT /v1/roles/{role_id}. CONFIRMED 200 2026-06-24: updates description (non-destructive). Restores description to original value from capture_soft (or API regression suite marker).

steps.name: set-role-trust-policy
steps._note: setroletrustpolicy — PUT /v1/roles/{role_id}/trust-policy. CONFIRMED 200 2026-06-24. Restores the exact trust policy currently in place (sts:* from Principal Account 73eab1a74c6347c1be9c892efc7f1102). Non-destructive because it re-applies the same trust policy that already exists.

steps.name: restore-role-description
steps._note: Restore the original role description. PUT with empty string (API doesn't accept null, returns 200 but keeps previous value if null passed).

steps.name: delete-temp-policy
steps._note: Explicit delete of temp policy in lifecycle steps (not just cleanup block). Belt-and-suspenders: ensures the policy is unbound from the role before deletion. Cleanup block also deletes it, making this idempotent (second delete returns 404 which is fine).

lifecycles._note: Light. Covers policy write ops NOT covered by the base iam-policy lifecycle: PUT /v1/policies/{policy_id}, PUT /v1/policies/{policy_id}/bindings, plus the user/group policy-binding add/remove and resource-policy statement ops. A real USER_DEFINED policy is created (group 'pol-real', body from createpolicy with server-assigned id fields omitted) then set/bound/deleted; all sub-steps optional so a 4xx records coverage. Create envelope is FLAT $.id (confirmed from createpolicy 201 doc example, same as base iam-policy). SAFETY (Hard Rule 3): the 'pol-bulk' group exercising DELETE /v1/policies/bulk (management/iam/deletepolicies) was REMOVED — verified on live runs #124 (unmatched synthetic id) AND #125 (a valid OWNED id, body $.id correct) that the SCP backend IGNORES the policy_ids body entirely and fans the call out into a delete-ALL-account-policies attempt (#125: 422 policy.delete.start over 832 attempts / 417 delete.error across 237 distinct NON-test system policies — AdministratorAccess_ACL, ObjectStorageAccess, PaaSCommon-*, …). No request body makes this endpoint safe; it is un-probeable and waived (data/baselines/coverage_waivers.json, class blast-radius).

steps.name: set-policy
steps._note: setpolicy: server-assigned version id fields omitted; updates name/description/document.

steps.name: set-policy-bindings
steps._note: setpolicygroupbinding: add/remove a synthetic GROUP id -> expected 400/404 but PUT is CALLED.

steps.name: query-policy
steps._note: querypolicy — POST /v1/policies/list. Standalone (not group-gated so it fires even if pol-real fails). All query and body params optional; excluded_policy_ids is a best-effort filter only. Confirmed 200 on this account (runtime_status run, count=27 policies). Body from api_bodies.json (querypolicy). Closes GAP-mut for management/iam/querypolicy via the lifecycle file (also wired in scenarios.json xcov-querypolicy group but lives here for the iam-lifecycle batch).

lifecycles._note: Light. Covers group member + policy-binding write ops: POST/DELETE /v1/groups/{group_id}/members, POST/DELETE /v1/groups/{group_id}/policy-bindings. Creates a real group AND a real policy (both in group 'grp-bind') so addgrouppolicybinding uses a real policy_id (-> 200 instead of 404). Member ops still use synthetic user_id (no IAM users on account) -> 404, but CALLED. Group create envelope $.group.id confirmed; policy create envelope $.id (flat, confirmed). setgroup REQUIRES 'name' field (CONFIRMED 2026-06-23). Policy cleaned up in cleanup block; group cleaned up by delete-group step AND cleanup block (belt-and-suspenders).

steps.name: create-policy-for-group
steps._note: createpolicy: create a real USER_DEFINED policy so addgrouppolicybinding can bind a real policy_id to the group (vs 404 with synthetic id). Flat capture $.id confirmed from createpolicy 201 doc. Cleaned up by cleanup block.

steps.name: set-group
steps._note: setgroup — PUT /v1/groups/{group_id}. CONFIRMED 2026-06-23: body REQUIRES 'name' field (400 'Field required' without it). Captures group_name from create response ($.group.name) and re-sends it unchanged with new description.

steps.name: add-group-member
steps._note: addgroupmember: synthetic user_id -> 404 (no IAM users on account), POST is CALLED and catalog key recorded.

steps.name: add-group-policy-binding
steps._note: addgrouppolicybinding: uses real policy_id captured from create-policy-for-group -> CONFIRMED 200 (real policy bind). Falls back gracefully if policy create 503'd.

steps.name: remove-group-policy-binding
steps._note: removegrouppolicybinding: uses real grp_policy_id captured above -> CONFIRMED 204 (removes the real policy binding). Falls back gracefully if policy not bound.

steps.name: remove-group-member
steps._note: removegroupmember: synthetic user id -> 404 (no real member), DELETE is CALLED and catalog key recorded.

lifecycles._note: Light, standalone (no resource create). Covers POST/DELETE /v1/users/{user_id}/policy-bindings against a synthetic user id so both writes are CALLED. A synthetic user id yields 400/404 (user not found) but coverage is recorded on the call. adduserpolicybinding body from api_bodies.json (policy_ids).

steps.name: get-user-policy-bindings
steps._note: id-bound read (listuserpolicybindings). CONFIRMED 2026-06-20: GET /v1/users/{user_id}/policy-bindings returns 200 with ANY user_id, even a fully-synthetic all-zeros id — the IAM gateway returns an empty list rather than 404 for unknown users. {unique} will therefore hit 200 here (smoke-verified via direct ApiClient probe). Path normalizes to catalog key management/iam/listuserpolicybindings via '*' segment.

lifecycles._note: Light, standalone. Covers the resource-policy write ops: PUT/DELETE /v1/resource-policies/{srn}, POST /v1/resource-policies/{srn}/statements, PUT/DELETE /v1/resource-policies/{srn}/statements/{sid}. KEY FIX (2026-06-20): the iam gateway decodes {srn} path segments as base64 — plain SRN yields 400 'SRN decoding error'; segment MUST be base64-encoded. KEY FIX (2026-06-23): Action in resource-based policy body MUST match the target resource's service (iam:* 400s 'UnSupportedActionInPolicy'; * also 400s; kms:* confirmed 200 against a KMS SRN). Strategy: filter resourcemanager list by resource_type=kms so the captured SRN is always from the kms service, then use kms:* action. Cleanup: setresourcepolicy creates a real policy -> deleteresourcepolicy MUST run as cleanup (destructive). Also: setpermission/removepermission need the real Sid used in addpermission; both use literal 'Statement2' which matches the addpermission body. VALIDATED 2026-06-23: setresourcepolicy 200, showresourcepolicy 200, addpermission 201 (kms:*), setpermission 200, removepermission 204, deleteresourcepolicy 204.

steps.name: list-kms-resources
steps._note: Soft-capture a KMS SRN (resource_type=kms filter confirmed 200 with 20 kms resources 2026-06-23). KMS SRN required because resource-based policy Action must match service — kms:* is confirmed valid. Without KMS filter, first resource might be vpc/secretsmanager/etc. which caused 400 UnSupportedActionInPolicy on prior runs. If 403 or empty, iam_srn stays unresolved -> b64-encode skipped -> placeholder SRN (catalog '*' key still covered).

steps.name: b64-encode-iam-srn
steps._note: Base64-encode the captured KMS SRN for use in /v1/resource-policies/{srn} path segments. REQUIRED: the iam gateway decodes {srn} path segments as base64. Mirrors b64-encode-srn in management__resourcemanager.json.

steps.name: set-resource-policy
steps._note: setresourcepolicy — PUT /v1/resource-policies/{srn}. CONFIRMED 200 2026-06-23: kms:* action is valid for a KMS SRN. Creates a resource policy (group 'rp-real'; cleanup deletes it). Action changed from iam:* (400 UnSupportedActionInPolicy) to kms:* (200). Expect_status narrowed to [200,201,202]: we now have confirmed 2xx.

steps.name: probe-resource-policy-reads
steps._note: showresourcepolicy — probe GET /v1/resource-policies/{srn}. CONFIRMED 200 2026-06-23. Explicitly maps catalog param 'srn' to the b64-encoded SRN value (iam_srn_b64). Without this explicit mapping, probe_reads can't resolve {srn} (ctx has 'iam_srn_b64', not 'srn'; _PARAM_ALIASES only has 'rg_srn' for srn). The probe fires GET /v1/resource-policies/{iam_srn_b64} after setresourcepolicy created the policy -> 200. Records under catalog key management/iam/showresourcepolicy. Group rp-real gates this on setresourcepolicy success.

steps.name: add-resource-policy-statement
steps._note: addpermission — POST /v1/resource-policies/{srn}/statements. CONFIRMED 201 2026-06-23 with kms:* action. Soft-captures $.Statement.Sid ('Statement2') as rp_statement_sid for use in setpermission/removepermission path. Action changed from iam:* to kms:* (same fix as setresourcepolicy).

steps.name: set-resource-policy-statement
steps._note: setpermission — PUT /v1/resource-policies/{srn}/statements/{sid}. CONFIRMED 200 2026-06-23. {rp_statement_sid} captured from addpermission response ($.Statement.Sid='Statement2'). Prior {unique} caused 404 because synthetic id didn't match created Sid. {rp_statement_sid} path segment normalizes to catalog '*' key (variable, not literal).

steps.name: remove-resource-policy-statement
steps._note: removepermission — DELETE /v1/resource-policies/{srn}/statements/{sid}. CONFIRMED 204 2026-06-23. {rp_statement_sid} captured from addpermission (same fix as setpermission).

steps.name: delete-resource-policy
steps._note: deleteresourcepolicy — DELETE /v1/resource-policies/{srn}. CONFIRMED 204 2026-06-23. Also registered as cleanup on set-resource-policy step (belt-and-suspenders so teardown runs even if this explicit step is skipped).

lifecycles._note: HEAVY (irreversible/credential + account-user + SAML ops). Runs only under SCP_RUN_HEAVY. Covers: POST/PUT/DELETE /v1/access-keys (+ bulk + send-otp); POST/PUT/DELETE /v1/accounts/{account_id}/users (+ bulk) and PUT .../password; POST/PUT/DELETE /v1/saml-providers (+ bulk). These create real credentials / users / federation providers, so each is optional with a broad expect_status: on a shared account most return 403 (permission) or 400 (body/account scope) which still records coverage on the CALL. {account_id} uses a synthetic id; access-key/saml ids likewise synthetic for the PUT/DELETE-by-id steps. createsamlprovider/setsamlprovider bodies in api_bodies.json are corrupt (_raw stringified) -> we send a best-effort multipart-less JSON guess; marked NOT runtime-proven. accesskeycreate parent_access_key_id/passcode omitted (account-specific). RISK: every step here is unproven against a real 2xx; the goal is purely to CALL each write endpoint so a future live run records it.

steps.name: access-key-send-otp
steps._note: accesskeysendtemporaryotp: sends an OTP to the caller; safe-ish but gated heavy because it triggers a real notification.

steps.name: create-access-key
steps._note: accesskeycreate: PERMANENT key. parent_access_key_id/passcode omitted. Captures id if returned; the PUT/DELETE-by-id steps fall back to a synthetic id when capture misses (separate group).

steps.name: set-access-key
steps._note: accesskeyset: enable/disable. Synthetic id ({unique}) so the PUT is always CALLED; path param segment normalizes to '*'.

steps.name: delete-access-keys-bulk
steps._note: Body access_key_ids from convention (no confirmed example) -> synthetic id.

steps.name: create-account-user
steps._note: createiamuser: empty group_ids/policy_ids; synthetic account_id ({unique}) -> expected 400/403/404, POST CALLED. user_name unique.

steps.name: update-account-user
steps._note: updateiamuser.

steps.name: set-account-user-password
steps._note: updateiamuserpassword. password omitted-as-empty to avoid setting a weak real password; expecting 400/403.

steps.name: delete-account-users-bulk
steps._note: Body user_ids from convention (no confirmed example) -> synthetic id.

steps.name: create-saml-provider
steps._note: createsamlprovider: api_bodies.json entry is corrupt (_raw). Best-effort JSON guess (name + metadata_document placeholder); NOT runtime-proven. Likely 400 on invalid metadata, which still records coverage. Soft-captures saml_provider_id ($.id, FLAT envelope per the doc 201 example) to drive the id-bound show below; on the expected 4xx nothing is captured and the show segment stays a placeholder.

steps.name: show-saml-provider
steps._note: id-bound read (showsamlprovider). Closes GAP-get-id for GET /v1/saml-providers/{saml_provider_id}. Keys off the create-soft-captured saml_provider_id; tolerant [200,400,403,404] because the create body is UNPROVEN (corrupt api_bodies.json entry) and 4xx's, leaving saml_provider_id a placeholder (normalizes to the catalog '*' key, still records coverage). HEAVY-gated with the rest of this lifecycle; the GET is CALLED so the endpoint is statically reachable.

steps.name: set-saml-provider
steps._note: setsamlprovider: corrupt body in api_bodies.json; best-effort guess; synthetic id.

steps.name: delete-saml-providers-bulk
steps._note: deletesamlproviders: CONFIRMED body key is 'ids' (not 'saml_provider_ids') from api_docs.json request_example 2026-06-24. Synthetic id -> 404 ResourceNotFound (vs 400 ValidationError with empty array or wrong key). Not coverable to 2xx without a real SAML provider (createsamlprovider requires multipart/form-data or HEAVY opt-in).

lifecycles._note: Light, READ-ONLY (no writes, no cleanup). Closes 4 static id-bound GET gaps for read-only / list-discoverable IAM resources by the list->soft-capture->show idiom (the same pattern cloudcontrol uses for its list-discovered ids). access-keys and service-accounts have only list+show in the catalog (no create), so a synthetic id would be a guaranteed-404 dead read — instead we soft-capture a REAL id from the caller's own list and show it. account-users is shown via the account_id soft-captured from the caller's access-keys list (access_key.account_id) + a user id from the account-users list itself. Every step is optional with tolerant [200,400,403,404]: on an account with no access keys / service accounts the list is empty/403 and the dependent id segment stays a {placeholder} (normalizes to the catalog '*' key) so the show is still CALLED and the endpoint statically reachable. Envelopes grounded in data/api_docs.json response examples: accesskeylist $.access_keys[].{id,account_id}; listserviceaccount $.service_accounts[].id; listiamuser $.users[].id.

steps.name: list-access-keys
steps._note: Zero-param list (already in the smoke GET floor) reused here to soft-capture a REAL access_key_id + the caller's account_id (accesskeylist envelope $.access_keys[]). Drives the two id-bound shows below.

steps.name: show-access-key
steps._note: id-bound read (accesskeyshow). Closes GAP-get-id for GET /v1/access-keys/{access_key_id}. Keys off the list-captured access_key_id (a real id when the caller has any key); if none, the segment stays a placeholder (normalizes to catalog '*') and 4xx's. Tolerant [200,400,403,404]; the GET is CALLED so the endpoint is statically reachable.

steps.name: list-account-users
steps._note: id-bound read (listiamuser) — Closes GAP-get-id for GET /v1/accounts/{account_id}/users. account_id is soft-captured from list-access-keys (the caller's own account); the segment normalizes to catalog '*'. Also soft-captures a real user id ($.users[].id) to drive show-account-user. Tolerant [200,400,403,404].

steps.name: show-account-user
steps._note: id-bound read (showiamuser). Closes GAP-get-id for GET /v1/accounts/{account_id}/users/{user_id}. Both segments are placeholders (account_id from list-access-keys, account_user_id from list-account-users) -> normalizes to v1/accounts/*/users/* matching the catalog. If either is uncaptured the show 4xx's harmlessly while still recording coverage. Tolerant [200,400,403,404].

steps.name: list-service-accounts
steps._note: Zero-param list (smoke GET floor) reused to soft-capture a REAL service_account_id (listserviceaccount envelope $.service_accounts[]). Drives show-service-account.

steps.name: show-service-account
steps._note: id-bound read (showserviceaccount). Closes GAP-get-id for GET /v1/service-accounts/{service_account_id}. service-accounts is read-only in the catalog (list+show only, no create), so a synthetic id would be a guaranteed-404 dead read — instead this keys off the list-captured real service_account_id. If the caller has no service accounts the segment stays a placeholder (normalizes to catalog '*') and 4xx's. Tolerant [200,400,403,404].

steps.name: delete-account-users-bulk-empty
steps._note: deletebulkiamuser (DELETE /v1/accounts/{account_id}/users/bulk). CONFIRMED 2026-06-24: empty user_ids array [] returns 204 (idempotent, no users deleted). account_id is soft-captured from list-access-keys (the caller's own real account id). This is NON-HEAVY because no IAM users are created or deleted — the empty array is a no-op. Covers the catalog key management/iam/deletebulkiamuser.
